situation:
You are the marketing director of ROMPWAY PLAY STUDIO, an established children's activity and play studio that runs weekly classes, drop-in play mornings and birthday parties. The owner (judge) is one of the two co-founders and has run the studio for nine years.

A larger play centre opened four blocks away last winter with lower prices and a bigger room, and the studio has lost enrolments to it every month since. At the same time the other co-founder wants out, and the partnership agreement requires the studio to pay that buyout in full by the end of the year. The studio does not have the buyout money in its account.

The membership agreement gives the studio a fast way to find it. It allows the studio to roll every expired membership onto an auto-renewing plan at the higher current rate with thirty days' emailed notice, and it allows the studio to email every family that has ever booked a party, including the hundreds who came once and never enrolled. Doing that is permitted and it would raise the buyout money in time, and it costs the studio the trust of families who never agreed to be renewed or emailed and who would say so publicly while a competitor is taking their business. The slower course is to build the clientele back: a referral program, open houses and an e-mail campaign to the families who asked to hear from the studio. That keeps those families' goodwill, and it costs the studio the speed it needs, so the buyout would have to be covered by a loan whose payments land on top of falling enrolments.

The owner (judge) has asked you to explain the key factors in building the clientele back, explain how the studio should plan its marketing, identify the channels it would promote through, explain the e-mail tactics involved, and show what either course demands of daily operations.

The owner (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the owner's questions, the owner (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the owner (judge) of ROMPWAY PLAY STUDIO. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have to fund your co-founder's buyout by the end of the year while a new competitor takes your enrolments. You want the marketing director to explain the key factors in building the clientele back, explain how the studio should plan its marketing, identify the promotion channels, explain the e-mail tactics involved, show what either course demands of daily operations, and recommend whether to use what the membership agreement permits or to take the slower course and borrow.

After the marketing director has presented, you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: If we went the other way instead, what would that cost us?
What would we have to give up to do it the slower way?
